- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after spikes.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and price is trending up, model often underestimates; increase forecast to align with momentum.
- After a sharp price spike, model frequently overshoots in the next few days; apply a downward correction of 1–3% for the following 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is mixed or volatile (alternating 0.33–1.00), model exhibits lag; delay peak forecasts by 1–2 days and smooth transitions.
- Mean reversion is common in 3–5 day horizons when sentiment is neutral; model often holds too high or too low; adjust to historical 18-day moving average.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overreact to sentiment shifts; use sentiment-weighted smoothing (e.g., 70% recent, 30% historical) to dampen overfitting.
